mainTopic: The עולה and the יסוד; the 'lazy group'; rinsing the עזרה on שבת; and רבי יהודה's cup of mixed blood
overview: This amud finishes a short derivation and then explains several lines of the משנה about the קרבן פסח. First, a פסוק shows that a קרבן עולה needs its blood placed where the מזבח has a יסוד. Next, a ברייתא calls the third group the 'lazy group.' The גמרא explains that although a third group was needed, each person should have hurried to be in an earlier one, as רבי teaches that a necessary role can still be less fortunate. The גמרא then asks who objected to the כהנים rinsing the עזרה floor on שבת. רב חסדא says it was רבי אליעזר, who treats sprinkling a floor as a Torah-level מלאכה. רב אשי says it could even be the חכמים, following רבי נתן, who permits only a necessary שבות in the מקדש. Finally, the גמרא examines רבי יהודה's cup of mixed blood. It defends the cup against two objections: that the floor blood was never received in a כלי, and that דם התמצית is mixed in. Then it brings רבי אלעזר's statement that even רבי יהודה agrees דם התמצית does not bring כפרה, and this challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Where do we learn the rule for the burnt-offering itself?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that an עולה needs its blood placed against the יסוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the עולה itself, from where do we learn it?
steps.whatsHappening: Just before this, the גמרא learned a rule about the יסוד by comparing it to the עולה. Now it asks for the source of that rule for the עולה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A comparison only works if the original case has a solid source. Here the גמרא checks the base of its own argument: how do we know that the עולה needs the יסוד?

keyTerms.meaning: Burnt-offering, which is burned completely on the מזבח
From where do we know it?

phrases.english: And the burnt-offering itself — from where do we know it?
phrases.notes: The question is about the requirement of the יסוד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the derivation on the previous amud by asking for the source of the base case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source that an עולה needs blood placement where there is a יסוד.

steps.title: The verse links the base of the altar to the burnt-offering
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק calls it 'the יסוד of the מזבח of the עולה,' which shows that an עולה needs the יסוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'At the base of the altar of the burnt-offering.' This shows that an עולה needs the base.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק that names the מזבח's יסוד together with the עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse is speaking about a different קרבן, yet it describes the מזבח as 'the altar of the עולה' right next to the word יסוד. The גמרא reads that connection as a sign that the עולה requires the יסוד.

keyTerms.meaning: The base, a ledge at the bottom of the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: An עולה requires the יסוד, based on the phrase 'יסוד מזבח העולה.'

phrases.english: The verse said:
'At the base of the altar of the burnt-offering'
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק in ויקרא ד:ז.

phrases.english: Apparently, a burnt-offering requires the base.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: אֶל יְסוֹד מִזְבַּח הָעוֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrase 'יסוד מזבח העולה' ties the יסוד to the עולה.

steps.title: The third group is called the lazy group
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about the groups that bring the קרבן פסח, and a ברייתא that calls the third group lazy.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The first group went out, etc.' It was taught: it is called the lazy group.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה about the three groups that brought the קרבן פסח. It quotes a ברייתא saying the third group was called 'the lazy group.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קרבן פסח was slaughtered in three groups, one after the other. The last group got its name because its members came last.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: 'The first group went out, etc.'
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the משנה here.

phrases.english: It was taught: it [the third group] is called the lazy group.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The third group of the קרבן פסח is called the lazy group.

steps.title: Why blame them if a third group was needed anyway?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the name: there had to be a third group, so what could its members have done differently?
steps.simpleTranslation: But it could not work without this! What should they have done?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the name 'lazy.' The system needs a third group, so someone has to be in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קרבן פסח has to be brought in three groups, so a last group cannot be avoided. Calling them lazy seems unfair if they were only filling a required role.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not possible / it would not be enough

phrases.english: But it is impossible without this [a third group],
what should they have done?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא quoted in step 3.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A third group is required, so being in it cannot be a fault.

steps.title: They still should have rushed to be earlier
steps.stepSummary: Even so, each person should have hurried to get into an earlier group.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so, they should have pushed themselves to hurry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that although a third group must exist, each person should still have tried to be in an earlier one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The criticism is not of the group's existence. It is of the individuals who did not make the effort to come early. The system needs a last group, but no one should aim to be in it.

keyTerms.meaning: To make themselves hurry / be eager

phrases.english: Even so,
they should have made themselves hurry.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ הָכִי, אִיבְּעִי לְהוּ לְזָרוֹזֵי נַפְשַׁיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Separates the need for the role from each person's duty to be eager
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A required role cannot deserve criticism.
steps.terutzMaskana: The role is required, but each individual should still have tried to avoid being last.

steps.title: רבי: necessary roles can still be less fortunate
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא from רבי shows that the world needs certain roles, yet some are happier to have than others.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי says, the world cannot exist without a perfume seller and without a tanner. Fortunate is the one whose trade is perfume; woe to the one whose trade is tanning. And the world cannot exist without males and without females. Fortunate is the one whose children are males; woe to the one whose children are females.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports its answer with a ברייתא. It shows that something can be necessary for the world and still be less desirable for the person who has it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A tanner is needed, but his work smells bad, so his lot is less pleasant than a perfumer's. In the same way, a third group is needed, but no one should want to be in it. The line about sons and daughters reflects the hardships of raising daughters in that society, such as dowry and protection, not a judgment about their value.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
Tanner of hides, a smelly trade

steps.whatToRemember: Being needed does not make a role desirable. Each person should still try for the better role, so the third group is fairly called the 'lazy group.'

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rebbi says:

phrases.aramaic: אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְעוֹלָם בְּלֹא בַּסָּם וּבְלֹא בּוּרְסִי.
phrases.english: The world cannot exist without a perfume seller and without a tanner.
Fortunate is he whose trade is perfume,
woe to him whose trade is tanning.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְעוֹלָם בְּלֹא זְכָרִים וּבְלֹא נְקֵבוֹת.
phrases.english: And the world cannot exist without males and without females.
Fortunate is he whose children are males,
woe to him whose children are females.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for the answer in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: A necessary role can still be a less fortunate one.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי about the perfumer and the tanner, and about sons and daughters.

steps.title: Against whose wishes was the floor rinsed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's phrase 'not with the consent of the חכמים' and asks which sage is meant.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Like its procedure on a weekday, etc.' Not with the consent of whom?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to another line of the משנה: on שבת the כהנים rinsed the עזרה floor of blood 'not with the consent of the חכמים.' It asks which חכם objected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'חכמים' usually mean the majority, but here that seems hard. The גמרא wants to identify exactly which opinion forbids the rinsing, and step 8 explains why it cannot be the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Like its procedure on a weekday

phrases.english: 'Like its procedure on a weekday, etc.'
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the משנה, which ends: 'the כהנים rinse the עזרה, not with the consent of the חכמים.'

phrases.english: Not with the consent of whom?

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַעֲשֵׂהוּ בַּחוֹל וְכוּ׳. שֶׁלֹּא בִּרְצוֹן מַאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: the next line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which sage opposed rinsing the עזרה floor on שבת.

steps.title: It means רבי אליעזר, since the רבנן would permit it
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the objector is רבי אליעזר. For the רבנן, rinsing is only a שבות, and a שבות does not apply in the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Not with the consent of רבי אליעזר. For if it were the רבנן, they say rinsing is only a שבות, and there is no שבות in the מקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא identifies the objector as רבי אליעזר. He proves it by showing that the רבנן would have no reason to object.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן hold that rinsing the floor is only a rabbinic prohibition, a שבות. Rabbinic שבת prohibitions were not imposed in the מקדש, so the רבנן would allow it. Only רבי אליעזר, who treats it as more serious, would oppose it.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who answers the question
Rabbinic שבת prohibitions do not apply in the מקדש

steps.whatToRemember: 'Not with the consent of the חכמים' here means רבי אליעזר. According to the רבנן, rinsing in the מקדש on שבת is allowed because אין שבות במקדש.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume 'חכמים' here means the majority. רב חסדא shows it must refer to a single sage, רבי אליעזר.
steps.whyThisMatters: This uses the general rule אין שבות במקדש, which comes up throughout ש״ס.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
Not with the consent of Rabbi Eliezer.
For if it were the Rabbis —
don't they say it is only a rabbinic prohibition,
and there is no rabbinic prohibition in the Temple.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: שֶׁלֹּא בִּרְצוֹן רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The objector is רבי אליעזר, because for the רבנן it is a שבות, and אין שבות במקדש.

steps.title: The source: רבי אליעזר treats sweeping and sprinkling as real מלאכות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where רבי אליעזר's view comes from and quotes a ברייתא. In it, רבי אליעזר rules that sweeping, sprinkling water on a floor, and removing honeycombs are Torah-level מלאכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the source? As a ברייתא teaches: someone who milks, curdles milk, or makes cheese is liable for the size of a dried fig. Someone who sweeps, sprinkles water on the floor, or removes honeycombs is liable as follows. If he did it by mistake on שבת, he must bring a חטאת. If he did it on purpose on יום טוב, he gets forty lashes. These are the words of רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רב חסדא's answer from step 8 by showing the ברייתא where רבי אליעזר treats floor-sprinkling as a real Torah-level מלאכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rinsing the floor is like sprinkling water on it (מרבץ). רבי אליעזר holds that this is a full Torah-level מלאכה, serious enough to require a חטאת or lashes. The מקדש permits only what the קרבנות truly require, and a clean floor is not one of those things. So by רבי אליעזר's view, rinsing the floor on שבת would be forbidden even in the מקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: One who sprinkles water on a floor to settle the dust
Sin-offering brought for breaking a Torah-level שבת law by mistake
Receives the Torah punishment of (forty) lashes

steps.confusionAlert: The milking and cheese-making lines are just part of the same ברייתא. The part that matters for our משנה is the line about sweeping and sprinkling, because rinsing the floor counts as sprinkling.

phrases.english: What is it (the source)?
As it was taught in a ברייתא:
Whether one milks, or curdles milk, or makes cheese
is liable for the size of a dried fig.
One who sweeps or sprinkles water on the floor
or removes honeycombs
by mistake on Shabbat
is obligated to bring a sin-offering;
if he did it on purpose on a Festival
he receives the forty lashes;
these are the words of Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for רב חסדא's claim that רבי אליעזר treats rinsing as a Torah-level prohibition.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's claim that the 'חכמים' who objected to rinsing the floor is רבי אליעזר
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where רבי אליעזר makes sweeping and sprinkling liable for a חטאת on שבת and lashes on יום טוב

steps.title: The חכמים say sweeping and sprinkling are only a שבות
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends with the חכמים, who hold that these acts are forbidden only by rabbinic law, whether on שבת or on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: in both cases, on שבת and on יום טוב, it is forbidden only because of a שבות.
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes the ברייתא by giving the opposing view of the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the חכמים, sprinkling and sweeping are only a שבות (a rabbinic prohibition). A שבות does not apply in the מקדש. So by their view, rinsing the floor would be fine there, which is why רב חסדא said the objector must be רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this case and that case (here: שבת and יום טוב)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר holds that sprinkling a floor is Torah-level, so it is forbidden in the מקדש. The חכמים hold it is a שבות, so it is permitted in the מקדש. This is רב חסדא's explanation.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
both this (Shabbat) and that (Festival)
are forbidden only because of a rabbinic prohibition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא by showing the opposing view, which confirms רב חסדא's split.
steps.raayaObject: That only רבי אליעזר, and not the חכמים, would object to rinsing the floor in the מקדש
steps.raayaSupportSource: The חכמים's ruling in the same ברייתא that these acts are only a שבות

steps.title: רב אשי: the משנה can follow the חכמים, together with רבי נתן
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says we do not need to say the objector is רבי אליעזר. The משנה can follow the חכמים who see rinsing as a שבות, as understood through רבי נתן's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: you can even say 'not with the consent of the חכמים' refers to the חכמים who hold it is a שבות. The משנה follows רבי נתן.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers a different explanation of the משנה. He agrees that rinsing is only a שבות, yet still explains why it was not approved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא assumed that every שבות is permitted in the מקדש. רב אשי disagrees with that assumption. He says the משנה follows רבי נתן, who does not permit every שבות in the מקדש. That way, even the חכמים could object to rinsing the floor.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say (an alternative explanation)
Not with the consent of the Sages (the משנה's phrase)

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
You can even say 'not with the consent of the Sages' refers to the Rabbis
and the משנה follows Rabbi Natan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the question in step 7, as an alternative to רב חסדא's answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the משנה to a different תנא (רבי נתן) whose rule changes the outcome
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because a שבות does not apply in the מקדש, the objector must be רבי אליעזר, who sees rinsing as Torah-level.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even if rinsing is only a שבות, רבי נתן permits only a necessary שבות in the מקדש, so the חכמים could still object.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The objectors can be the חכמים themselves. The משנה follows רבי נתן, who permits only a necessary שבות in the מקדש, and rinsing the floor is not necessary.

steps.title: רבי נתן: only a necessary שבות was permitted in the מקדש
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא gives רבי נתן's rule. A שבות that is needed for the service was permitted in the מקדש, and one that is not needed was not.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches, רבי נתן says: a necessary שבות, they permitted. A שבות that is not necessary, they did not permit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the source for רב אשי's answer, which is רבי נתן's rule about a שבות in the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קרבנות can be offered properly even if the floor is not rinsed. That makes rinsing an 'unnecessary' שבות. Under רבי נתן's rule, then, it was not permitted, and that explains the משנה's phrase 'not with the consent of the חכמים.'

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic prohibition that must be broken for the Temple service
A rabbinic prohibition that is not needed for the service

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule limits the general idea that 'a שבות does not apply in the מקדש.' According to רבי נתן, the exception covers only what the service truly needs.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a ברייתא, Rabbi Natan says:
a necessary rabbinic prohibition, they permitted;
a rabbinic prohibition that is not necessary, they did not permit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the ברייתא that supports רב אשי's alternative answer.
steps.raayaObject: רב אשי's claim that the משנה can follow רבי נתן
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי נתן's ברייתא distinguishing a necessary שבות from an unnecessary שבות

steps.title: Why רבי יהודה had the כהן fill a cup with mixed blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה's line from the משנה, then cites a ברייתא explaining his reason. The cup of mixed blood protects against the case where one קרבן's blood spills.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'רבי יהודה says, he would fill a cup' and so on. A ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה says, he would fill a cup from the mixed blood on the floor. That way, if the blood of one of the קרבנות spilled, this cup would make that קרבן valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line in the משנה, רבי יהודה's cup of mixed blood, and brings a ברייתא that explains why he did it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sometimes the blood of a קרבן spills on the floor before it reaches the מזבח. That קרבן would then be invalid. The spilled blood mixes with the blood on the floor, so a cup filled from that mixture contains some of its blood. Throwing that cup on the מזבח makes the קרבן valid.

keyTerms.meaning: The mixed blood that collected on the floor of the עזרה

steps.confusionAlert: The cup is not a regular part of the service. It is a backup that is used only in case some קרבן's own blood spilled before it was thrown on the מזבח.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר כּוֹס הָיָה מְמַלֵּא וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: The משנה says: 'Rabbi Yehuda says: he would fill a cup,' etc.
It was taught in a ברייתא: Rabbi Yehuda says:
he would fill a cup from the mixed blood,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאִם יִשָּׁפֵךְ דָּמוֹ שֶׁל אֶחָד מֵהֶן
phrases.english: so that if the blood of one of them spilled
this cup would turn out to make it valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר כּוֹס הָיָה מְמַלֵּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the rinsing discussion and opens a new topic from the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה had a cup filled from the mixed blood so that any קרבן whose blood spilled could still be made valid with it.

steps.title: The Sages object that the floor blood was never received in a vessel
steps.stepSummary: Inside the ברייתא, the חכמים challenge רבי יהודה. The blood on the floor was never caught in a כלי, so it is not fit for זריקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to רבי יהודה: But wasn't this blood never received in a vessel?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues. The חכמים push back on רבי יהודה's cup of mixed blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood must be received in a כלי (קבלה) to be fit for the מזבח. Blood that went straight from the animal's neck to the floor never had קבלה. So, the חכמים argue, pouring it on the מזבח does nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: but isn't it so that...? (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: They said to Rabbi Yehuda:
But wasn't it not received in a vessel?
phrases.notes: Blood without קבלה in a כלי is not fit for the מזבח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The חכמים challenge the reason רבי יהודה gave in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's practice of using the floor blood as a backup
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Blood that was not received in a כלי is unfit, so the floor blood cannot serve as a backup.

steps.title: How could the Sages know the blood was not received?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the חכמים' wording. How could they know for sure that the blood was never caught in a כלי?
steps.simpleTranslation: How do they know?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops and questions the way the חכמים phrased their objection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים spoke as if they were certain the blood had no קבלה. No one can know that for sure, because some of the floor blood may have spilled from a כלי. So the גמרא will need to reread their words.

phrases.english: How do they know?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the certainty in the חכמים' objection.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Nobody can be sure that blood on the floor was never received in a כלי.

steps.title: Rereading the Sages' words as 'perhaps'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the חכמים meant 'perhaps it was not received in a כלי.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what they said to him: Perhaps it was not received in a vessel?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question by reading the חכמים' objection as a doubt instead of a certainty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים were not claiming to know. Their point was that there is a real chance the blood had no קבלה. Because of that doubt, the blood should not be used.

keyTerms.meaning: rather, this is what they said to him

phrases.english: Rather, this is what they said to him:
Perhaps it was not received in a vessel?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves step 15 by rereading the objection.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חכמים claimed certainty that there was no קבלה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חכמים only raised a doubt.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: I only meant blood that was received
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה answers that he only spoke about blood that was received in a כלי and then spilled.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: I too only spoke about blood that was received in a vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה answers the חכמים' objection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה agrees that blood without קבלה is unfit. He says the floor blood in his case did have קבלה and then spilled. So the cup is a valid backup.

phrases.english: He said to them:
I too did not say it
except about blood that was received in a vessel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן: אַף אֲנִי לֹא אָמַרְתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the חכמים' objection from steps 14 and 16.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה used blood that may never have had קבלה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה only meant blood that was received in a כלי and then spilled.

steps.title: How could רבי יהודה know the blood was received?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns the question around. How could רבי יהודה know the floor blood had קבלה?
steps.simpleTranslation: How does he know?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same kind of question it asked about the חכמים, but now about רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the חכמים cannot be sure the blood had no קבלה, then רבי יהודה cannot be sure it did. The floor blood is a mix, so his claim needs support.

phrases.english: How does he know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יהודה's answer in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's claim that the floor blood was received in a כלי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is no way to be sure that the floor blood ever had קבלה.

steps.title: כהנים are quick and careful
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that כהנים are זריזין, so they surely caught all the blood in a כלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: כהנים are vigilant.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יהודה using a known trait of כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We can assume כהנים did their job right and caught all the blood. So any blood on the floor must have spilled after קבלה.

phrases.english: Kohanim are vigilant.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A חזקה about how כהנים behave
steps.terutzHavaAmina: There is no basis to assume the floor blood had קבלה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since כהנים are careful, the blood was received first.

steps.title: If they are so careful, why did blood spill?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if כהנים are so careful, how did any blood spill at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: If they are vigilant, why does it spill?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea that כהנים are careful seems to clash with the whole case, which is about spilled blood. Careful people should not spill.

phrases.english: If they are vigilant —
why does it spill?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that כהנים are זריזין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Careful כהנים should not spill blood, yet the case assumes spilling.

steps.title: Their speed is what makes it spill
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the blood spills because the כהנים work so fast.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of the quickness with which they work, it spills.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the tension. Being quick and spilling go together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being זריז makes them catch every drop, and it also makes them move fast. Moving fast causes some received blood to spill. So the floor blood did have קבלה, and רבי יהודה's cup works.

keyTerms.meaning: because of, as a side effect of

steps.whatToRemember: The קבלה objection to רבי יהודה's cup is answered: the floor blood was received in a כלי first and spilled only because the כהנים worked fast. The גמרא raises a new problem with the cup, דם התמצית, in the next step.

phrases.english: Because of the quickness with which they work,
it spills.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Both traits come from the same cause
steps.terutzMaskana: Their speed causes spills after קבלה.

steps.title: But squeezed-out blood is mixed in
steps.stepSummary: A new problem: the floor blood includes דם התמצית, the blood that drips out after the main spurt. That blood is not fit for the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't דם התמצית mixed into it?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new attack on רבי יהודה's cup.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if some floor blood had קבלה, it is mixed with blood that dripped out slowly after the main spurt. That slow blood is not the 'life blood.' So the cup seems to contain unfit blood.

keyTerms.meaning: blood that drips out after the main spurt of שחיטה

phrases.english: But isn't the squeezed-out blood
mixed into it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the קבלה problem is solved, the גמרא raises a different problem with the same cup.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using the floor blood mixture for זריקה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The mixture contains דם התמצית, which is unfit for the מזבח.

steps.title: רבי יהודה holds squeezed-out blood is real blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יהודה follows his own view that דם התמצית is fully proper blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה follows his own reasoning, for he says: דם התמצית is proper blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יהודה by pointing to his own view in another place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, the slow dripping blood counts as real blood. So mixing it in does not ruin the cup.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda follows his own reasoning,
for he says: squeezed-out blood —
is proper blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Linking to the speaker's view elsewhere
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי יהודה, דם התמצית is real blood.

steps.title: Proof: רבי יהודה gives כרת for eating squeezed-out blood
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows the dispute. The תנא קמא says eating דם התמצית is a plain לאו. רבי יהודה says it carries כרת, like regular blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: דם התמצית is a warning (a לאו). רבי יהודה says: it carries כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that רבי יהודה treats דם התמצית as real blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating real 'life blood' carries כרת. Since רבי יהודה gives כרת for דם התמצית, he must see it as full blood. This backs up step 23.

keyTerms.meaning: a Torah warning (a לאו, punished with מלקות)
as it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: As it was taught:
squeezed-out blood is under a warning,
Rabbi Yehuda says: it is under karet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for step 23.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה's view that דם התמצית is proper blood
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where רבי יהודה gives כרת for eating דם התמצית

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: even רבי יהודה agrees it does not atone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer. רבי אלעזר said that even רבי יהודה agrees דם התמצית does not bring כפרה, based on a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי אלעזר say: רבי יהודה agrees that for כפרה it does not atone, as it says, 'For the blood atones by means of the life'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of steps 23 and 24 using a statement of רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה may treat דם התמצית as real blood for the איסור of eating. But רבי אלעזר says that for the מזבח only blood that carries the 'life' brings כפרה, and even רבי יהודה agrees. If so, the floor mixture still has unfit blood in it.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי אלעזר is saying רבי יהודה changed his mind about כרת. רבי יהודה still holds דם התמצית is real blood for eating. רבי אלעזר only says it does not work for כפרה on the מזבח.

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Elazar say:
Rabbi Yehuda agrees regarding atonement
that it does not atone,
as it is stated:
"For it is the blood that atones by means of the life,"
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק in ויקרא יז:יא. Only blood that the life leaves with brings כפרה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: מוֹדֶה רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in steps 23 and 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that רבי יהודה holds דם התמצית is proper blood
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even רבי יהודה agrees דם התמצית does not bring כפרה, so the mixture is still unfit for זריקה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This splits two areas of law. The same blood can be 'real blood' for the איסור of eating but not fit for כפרה on the מזבח.
